THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE  211

    There was something in the character and personalities of Mr. Halsell and his associates, and did they not strive to inculcate the idea of surrounding himself with competent and efficient men and women as teachers? I never knew of the old school to have created in the heart and mind of every pupil a desire to go forward in life and make the world better for having lived in it.

    The old school had another characteristic: it was a poor boy's and girl's school. There were no fancy and expensive frills to it. There was but one serious purpose, and that was to get an education. If any boy or girl failed to get an education from this school it was because he or she was unable to pay tuition. Although there was a strong effort Mr. Halsell always found way to provide tuition for those deserving it. I think of old this through his conversation instructed me that he was able to extend the advantages of the school to those who were not able to pay for it. Of this there were many who are here today, and they are grateful and honest.

    So, I again say, we are making history today in holding this reunion, and, for one, I am glad of the opportunity thus to pay tribute to the great men and women who made this school what it was.

    Much credit is due Ed McMahon for both the holding of this reunion and its success. He and I had long talks about this fine enterprise for several years, even before the death of our greatly beloved President and General Chairman, Warren Halsell. As a matter of fact, Ed and I made several visits when the construction of this gymnasium was under way, and when erected here as a suitable and fitting memorial to this noble man who is entitled to this fond memory. Even then my official duties were of such a onerous nature that I could not do more than assume more than a nominal relationship to the enterprise. The members of this Ex-Students body who planned, organized, raised funds, and spent their time and money in bringing the undertaking to its full fruition.
